message: `+` in the body of `handRolled`, which claims `restrict(no-wrap)`
help: Left shifts can discard high bits and are refused by `no-wrap`. `no-wrap` is LOCAL, like `no-cast`: on `Int` operands `+`, `-` and `*` lower to plain `add`/`sub`/`mul` with no overflow check, so a silent wraparound is an act this body performs by writing the raw operator, not a fact the effect row or call graph carries - it is refused where it is written, and a callee's arithmetic is the callee's claim to make. `stdlib/Err.ax` has the checked alternative for each: `addChecked`, `subChecked`, `mulChecked`, every one `(-> Int Int (Result Int Error))`. Calling one pulls `Alloc` into this body's effect row (constructing the `Result` allocates), so `no-wrap` cannot be satisfied together with `no-alloc` or `pure` by a body that needs arithmetic - write the checked call and match its `Err`, accept the row, or delete the tag. TWO OPERATORS ARE NOT REFUSED, because neither can wrap: the same three spellings on `Float` operands, which lower to `fadd`/`fsub`/`fmul`, and the `for` keyword's own counter increment, which the parser writes and whose loop guard bounds it
